title: Reflection AI Releases 501B Beam Weights as First Open Model
summary:
Reflection AI has published the weights, tokenizer, and reference implementation for Beam under an Apache 2.0 license, making the model available on Hugging Face. The release includes Mirror CLI, the open-source training harness Reflection used to build the model in collaboration with more than 40 partners. Designed for software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks, the model is now available for deployment across multiple platforms.

The mixture-of-experts model contains 501B total parameters and 23B active parameters with a 1M token context window. Trained on Nvidia GB300 NVL72 hardware, Beam delivers over 70K tokens per second per GPU on Blackwell Ultra. It has day-0 support from vLLM, SGLang, and Ollama, with the latter providing the model for free for a limited time. Artificial Analysis ranks Beam as the second-highest US open weights model on its Intelligence Index and the leading US open model on its Cyber Index.

selectedTweets.text:
Reflection’s first model, Beam, scores 30 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it #2 among US open weights models

Beam is an open weights model with 501B total and 23B active parameters, released on @huggingface 

Congratulations to @reflection_ai on the release!

Key takeaways:

➤ Second among US open weights models: Beam scores 30, behind only Meta's Muse Spark Open (39) and ahead of yesterday’s NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (26) release. Outside China, only Muse Spark Open and the UAE's K2 Horizon (31) score higher

➤ Token efficient for its intelligence: Beam uses ~26k output tokens per Intelligence Index task compared to K2 Horizon, one point ahead, which uses twice as many (~52k). Proprietary models still set the frontier, with GPT-6 Astra (max) scoring 53 on the same budget (~27k)

➤ Strong on agentic workflows, weaker in the terminal: Beam scores 48.5% on AutomationBench-AA, 11 percentage points ahead of K2 Horizon (37.2%) and level with Qwen3.8 27B (48.2%). Terminal-Bench 4.0 is a weak point, where Beam scores 3.0%, behind Qwen3.8 27B (5.6%) and Muse Spark Open (8.1%)

➤ Knows more, guesses more: On AA-Omniscience it answers 33% of questions correctly, well ahead of K2 Horizon (18%) and Qwen3.8 27B (16%). But its hallucination rate is 47%, against 26% for K2 Horizon and 30% for Qwen3.8 27B, giving Beam a net index score of 1.5, ahead of both peers (−3.0 and −10.0)

Other model details
Context window: 1M tokens
Modalities: Text
Parameters: 501B / 23B

selectedTweets.text:
Exciting news: Beam-1.0-501B-A23B by @Reflection_AI just landed #12 among open weight models in Agent Arena with -3.67% Net Improvement, and #22 among open in Code Arena: WebDev with 1438 pts. It’s also fully open under Apache 2.0.

On the Agent Arena leaderboard, Beam 1.0 is the top-ranked US model among open models, landing at #12. That puts it ahead of Hy3, MiMo V2.5 Pro and MiniMax M3. Its margin of error is wide (±3.84% on Net Improvement), so it’s statistically closer to the two Qwen3.8 models just above it than its rank suggests.

On Code Arena: WebDev, 24 of the top 25 open models come from Chinese labs. The one exception is Reflection’s Beam 1.0 (Apache 2.0). It ranks #22 among open models, which makes it the top US open model on the board, just ahead of Kimi K2.5 Thinking and GLM-5.

Congrats to the @Reflection_AI team on this solid open weights release!
